name: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Habitat)
description: Perseverance touched down here on 18 February 2021. In this demo it is the astronaut habitat: the default start point for every Marswalk.
importance: Mission base: start and end point for excursions.

source.label: Derived from the Perseverance traverse path (NASA/JPL-Caltech)

name: Jezero Crater
description: Measuring roughly 49 km in diameter, Jezero Crater formed during Mars’ Noachian period, approximately 4.1 to 3.7 billion years ago. At that time, liquid water flowed openly through channels across the surface of Mars, and pooled in lakes and seas. Jezero was once a great crater lake. Water accumulating from vast watersheds entered the lake through two inflow channels, one breaching the western rim and another flowing in from the north. Sediments gathered and concentrated in the inflowing rivers were deposited on the floor on the crater lake. Two delta deposit fans are visible where both of the inflow channels entered the crater, with the western deposit being the better preserved. Extending beyond the delta deposits are deeper basin fill deposits rich in carbonates. What appears to be an overlying volcanic deposit from the nearby Syrtis Major volcanic complex covers large areas of the central and eastern portions of the crater floor. A distinct outflow channel extends from the eastward edge of the crater. The northeastern half of the crater rim is heavily eroded, while the southwestern half remains prominent, rising over 800 meters above the crater floor.
importance: Context: an impact crater that once held a lake fed by river channels.

images.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (via NASA Mars Trek)

name: Western Delta Deposit
description: This fan of sedimentary material was deposited by the western inflow channel. It is particularly well preserved, exhibiting a finely layered structure that reveals its having been laid down over a prolonged period of time. It is rich in smectite clay and is a primary target for exploration by Perseverance.
importance: Top astrobiology target: layered, clay-rich lake delta sediments that could preserve biosignatures.

images.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (via NASA Mars Trek)
NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (via NASA Mars Trek)

name: Northern Delta Deposit
description: This fan of sedimentary material was deposited by the northern inflow channel. It is not as well defined as the western deposit. This deposit is dominated by magnesium-carbonates and associated olivine. A smaller tributary channel flowing from the southwest can be seen joining the main channel just before its entry into the lake.
importance: Second delta fan, useful for comparing sediment sources entering the lake.

images.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (via NASA Mars Trek)

name: Western Breach
description: This over 400-meter deep ravine is where the western inflow channel cut through the rim of Jezero Crater and filled the crater lake there. To the west of this ravine the channel extends westward draining a large watershed in the uplands above. To the east of the ravine, a large well-defined and clearly-layered delta deposit marks where the inflowing river dumped its burden of sand, clay rocks, and gravel. This breach remains quite prominent, as the crater rim here is relatively well-preserved, as opposed to in the locations of the northern inflow channel and the outflow channel to the east.
importance: Gap in the crater rim cut by inflowing water; exposes rim stratigraphy.

images.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (via NASA Mars Trek)

name: Western Inflow Channel
description: This river channel drained a vast watershed in the uplands extending to the west of Jezero Crater. It entered the crater through a gap in the western rim that is relatively well preserved compared to the northern inflow channel and to the outflow channel to the east. The inflowing channel left a remarkable delta deposit of sediment extending out across the western floor of the crater lakebed. The channel, once filled with flowing water, can now be seen to be occupied by extensive dunes of wind-blown sand.
importance: River valley that carried water and sediment into the lake (Neretva Vallis).

images.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (via NASA Mars Trek)

name: Northern Inflow Channel
description: Sava Vallis, the smaller of Jezero's two inflow valleys, entered the crater from the north and built the northern delta fan. Comparing its sediments with the western delta helps scientists understand how much of the lake's mud and sand came from each watershed.
importance: Northern river valley (Sava Vallis) feeding the lake; samples catchment rocks.
